summary: Gov. Jim Pillen (Republican) ran for re-election and won a second term over Lynne Walz (Democrat) and two minor-party candidates.

candidates.name: Jim Pillen
candidates.bio: Jim Pillen has been governor of Nebraska since 2023. President Trump endorsed him, and he ran with Lt. Gov. Joe Kelly.

positions.summary: Says the budget deficit should be solved with "durable, lasting tax cuts, not tax shifts," and wants lower property taxes and caps on local spending.
Supports school choice, including taxpayer-funded scholarships for private and parochial schools.
Turned the McCook work ethic camp into an ICE detention facility and has worked closely with the Trump administration.
Calls himself a "pro-life governor" and points to ending Medicaid subsidies for abortion providers.

candidates.name: Lynne Walz
candidates.bio: Lynne Walz is a former Nebraska state senator (2017-2025) and was the 2018 Democratic nominee for lieutenant governor.

positions.summary: Says she would balance the state budget first, broaden the tax base to keep taxes low, and provide targeted property tax relief.
Says education is under attack and pledges to stop it, and has voiced concern about public money going to private schools.
Lists accessible health care among her priorities.
Says voters' recent abortion decisions should be respected, and opposes limits on abortion in cases of rape, incest or to save the mother's life.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (MultiState governors tracker, updated Nov 4, 35 of 36 races called)
